How to play

Keyboard and mouse

  • A / D move, W or Space jump or swim up, S drop or dive
  • Click and hold to use the held item: mine, attack or place
  • 1–9 or wheel pick a hotbar slot
  • Tab bag, E grappling hook, H hide or show items, R army, F talk, trade, tame, cook or open chests, L aim lock, K quick save, G fly or walk in creative (and as the Scaleborn), hold B to breathe fire as the Scaleborn. You can change these in Settings.
  • Q change formation, M map, F trade or free a captive, Esc menu

Touch

  • Arrow pads move, jump, swim and dive
  • Tap and hold the world to use the held item, or switch to joysticks in Settings
  • Tap a villager or the Trade button to shop

New in Beta 0.9.162

Upgrading a shop from the task list (or anywhere the shop window is closed) works without an error.

New in Beta 0.9.161

The tool or weapon in your hand rests behind your character instead of across the face; it comes out in front when you swing, dig or shoot.

New in Beta 0.9.160

The tutorial ends with an army: after your miners arrive, the foreman shows you where their ore goes (the hut chest); you build on marked squares, raise a Small tower from the chest's stone, hire two soldiers, put them on the tower's posts, and then night falls and goblins raid. Trees in every world stand on flat ground, never on a slope.

New in Beta 0.9.159

The start screens are easier to use on phones and computers: every window has one close X, the title's buttons are bigger on phones held sideways, hints are easier to read, the room code box on the Multiplayer screen is wide again, and the wiki link is off the title screen (Help and the play site still have it).

New in Beta 0.9.158

Doors are always whole: a door is never half door and half stone, even in a ruined village. A chest set beside a door slides over to make room, and doors, workbenches, furnaces and chests always stand on level ground.

New in Beta 0.9.157

Workbenches, furnaces, chests and cupboards are always their full size, in every wood. Whatever sits in their space gives way: plants and loose pieces are cleared, and a block someone built comes out as an item to pick up. Doors, chests and other stations are never replaced.

New in Beta 0.9.156

Windows look like what you opened: a workbench's crafting window is made of that workbench's wood, the furnace is stone, a chest is planks of its own wood with iron corners, a barrel has iron hoops, and gold and sky chests have their own colours. Chests come in every wood (Spruce chest, Birch chest and more, made with that wood's planks). Every X is bigger and easier to hit. In the tutorial the Quartermaster rebuilds the village in about a minute while you do Elder Rowan's errand in the cave, and a tap on the tutorial card shows the whole task. The title screen links to a status page that lists outages and known problems.

New in Beta 0.9.155

On a phone held upright, the card asking you to turn it sideways has a Play upright button, for phones and apps that do not turn (the Claude app on a phone stays upright, so the card stayed up and the game looked like a black screen).

New in Beta 0.9.154

In the tutorial, the workbenches, furnaces and chests in the old village are their full size from the start, and digging into the ground shows a dirt or stone wall behind, as in a real world.

New in Beta 0.9.153

In the tutorial you meet Elder Rowan while the Quartermaster rebuilds the village. She asks for 5 stone from the little cave, so you mine it there and bring it back to her before you start building. The Tutorial screen fits a small phone, with every class in one row.

New in Beta 0.9.152

Dragon Amulet is played with the phone held sideways. Held upright, the game shows a card asking you to turn the phone and waits until you do. If you would rather play upright, Settings > Controls > Upright phone has Allow upright.

New in Beta 0.9.151

Blocks that need a stronger pickaxe tell you which one: aim a weaker pickaxe at them and a label shows the tier, swinging at them says what you need and what you have, and their item text names it too. Pickaxes go from tier 1 (wooden, copper, silver) through iron 2, gold 3, diamond 4, storm 5 and mythril 6 to adamantite 7, and each pickaxe's text starts with its tier.

New in Beta 0.9.150

Trees only grow on flat ground: a sapling can't go on a slope. Choosing a miner always gives the miners' hut its ore cart, bed and chest, so your miners can work and talk. In the tutorial the sea on both sides is the edge, the castle is rebuilt in a tenth of the usual time, both wanderers become miners, your first soldier comes from the Recruiter, the cave holds the stone and coal to mine, and new steps show farming (a hoe, tilling, planting) and taming an animal in the wild and leading it into a pen.

New in Beta 0.9.149

The tutorial world has rolling hills with trees, a beach and the ocean past each end, and a little cave in the hill to explore. New steps show you how to give two wanderers jobs (a miner and a soldier who joins your army) and how to tame an animal from the pen, and your soldier and pet help in the goblin fight.

New in Beta 0.9.148

The tutorial card is a little window: drag it anywhere by its title bar, pull its bottom-right corner to make it bigger or smaller, and scroll the task inside it. It remembers where you put it.

New in Beta 0.9.147

Continue lists only your own worlds. The test world and your scenes are under Test world, the worlds you played with friends are under Multiplayer, and the tutorial is under Tutorial. The tutorial card is smaller, its task scrolls like a page inside a short box, and Hide folds it to a small tab at the left that opens it again. While it is folded, each finished step tells you the next task in a message.

New in Beta 0.9.146

The tutorial card sits at the left under your bars, so it never covers the middle of the screen. Elder Rowan lives in the first village house, her chest stands between the first two houses, and the chest is the first thing you do after the castle is rebuilt.

New in Beta 0.9.145

New to the game? A Tutorial button sits under Multiplayer on the title screen, and the first time you press New game on a device the game offers it once. Pick a class and a tiny world walks you through walking, jumping, rebuilding the ruined castle with the Quartermaster (in under a minute there; a real world takes until the next day), mining, placing blocks, a chest, crafting a workbench and an iron pickaxe, a torch when night falls, eating, an errand for Elder Rowan and a fight with two goblins. A card at the top, like the one shown while you place a building, says one task at a time in the words of your keyboard or your phone's sticks and buttons and ticks itself off; a yellow arrow points the way. Tamed animals on their Pet job now fight beside you like your soldiers: they go for enemies near you or them, jump up to reach one and bite until it is down, and come back once the fight moves too far. Ore blocks keep the rock they were first seen in, however you dig around them. On a phone the Torch button no longer stops your tools: with it on, the pickaxe, axe, hoe and hammer work and a tap mines or builds, while a double-tap still places a torch. Skip step and Leave are always there, and the tutorial is saved in slot 7 so you can come back to it. Vorthax watches you: his eye follows the nearest player wherever you move, and he blinks every few seconds, a little more often when he perches. Placing a building takes two taps: the first shows a see-through picture of the building where it would go, green when it fits and red when something is in the way, and a second tap on it builds it. A quick double tap never builds. Tap somewhere else to move the picture; it goes away when the mouse leaves it, when you walk away, or with Esc or Cancel. A trebuchet boulder or a cannonball crashes on through any animal in its path, a hawk crossing its arc included, and still lands where you aimed. People, monsters and bosses stop it as before.

New in Beta 0.9.144

Vorthax moves: his body rides each wing beat, his head nods against it, a wave runs down his tail, his legs swing in flight and he breathes when he perches. His teeth are a neat row, his legs have a thigh, a shin and clawed feet, and when he breathes fire a flickering plume pours from his open jaws while the fire bolts fly as flames with a tail. In the scene editor, pinch on a phone or press the − and + buttons to zoom out far enough to see a whole scene.

New in Beta 0.9.143

The scene editor: on the title screen, Test world, then Scene editor opens a flat, empty world where everything is a sticker. Press Stickers and pick a block, a back wall, a slope, a plant or piece of furniture, a hero or soldier of any side, a villager, an enemy, an animal, a boss, Vorthax, a whole building or tree, or an item, then tap the world to put it there. Drag to paint blocks, right-click or use Erase to take things away. Select drags a box; Copy, Cut and Paste move it anywhere, as many times as you like; Fill box fills it with the block you hold; Undo and Redo go back and forward. Everyone stands still like a sticker until you press Move, and Reset puts every one back where you set it. Pick the time of day from the list, press Photo to save a picture, and Flatten all to start over. Nothing spawns, grows or attacks by itself. The scene saves in slot 6 and is back under Continue. Keys on a computer: P place, X erase, V select, O move, I stickers, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Delete.

New in Beta 0.9.142

Report a bug sends your report straight to the game's designer from any copy of the game: the web page, the phone, the apps. Write a line about what happened and press Send; the window thanks you and you carry on playing. A report written while offline is sent by itself the next time the game starts.

New in Beta 0.9.141

Fifty achievements. The new ones: mining each ore from coal to storm ore; crafting a workbench, a furnace, your first iron gear, a gem weapon, a bomb and 100 items in all; owning an adamantite piece and the top of every upgrade line; your first soldier, 10 and 20, a Veteran, 100 enemies defeated by your own hand, a war machine deployed, an enemy tower captured; a hut, watchtower, keep, pen and farmhouse built, 1,000 blocks placed, a shop at level 3; the sky realm, the magma realm, the deepstone and 10 world chests; 25 fish, an insect in the net, a tamed bird of prey. Worlds you already play count what you do from now on, and the ones that only look at the world (bosses, buildings standing, your army) count at once.

New in Beta 0.9.140

Achievements: thirteen of them, earned in every copy of the game and kept on this device. Rebuild the village, grow it into a town and a city, tame an animal, conquer a faction, and defeat each of the eight bosses. A toast and a sound mark a new one; the Achievements button on the title screen and in the pause menu shows them all as medals, grey until earned, with the day and the world. A world that already did these earns them when it loads. The test world never earns any.

New in Beta 0.9.139

The sixth class is called the Scaleborn (it was the Dragonborn), and his five weapons are the Scaleforged sword, bow, mace, staff and daggers. Nothing else about him changed: unlocks, saves and the weapons you already have carry over.

Seven items have new names and new pictures, with the same effects, recipes and shops: the Heart gem and Spirit gem (cut gems from the clusters in the magma realm; they were the life and mana crystals), the Bait pouch and Fisher's ring (fishing gear), the Fleetfoot sash (the dash), the Windstep boots, the Nautilus mask (breathe longer underwater) and the Merchant's charm (more coins). Anything you already own keeps working under its new name.

New in Beta 0.9.138

The Credits screen says what the game is made of: all its pictures and sounds come from its own code, the pixel font is Press Start 2P under the SIL Open Font License, and the libraries it uses are named.

New in Beta 0.9.137

Battle plans: walk up to Vorthax's lair, the Sky Ranger's hall or the Magma Knight's throne room with soldiers and choose how to attack. Ambush lets you place your soldiers on spots around the room; when the boss wakes they spring the trap, pinning Vorthax to the ground or stunning the knight or ranger for a few seconds while everyone strikes. Waves sends a few soldiers in at a time while the rest wait outside, and Charge takes everyone in together. Soldiers waiting or hiding still count as the army you brought.

Your soldiers run as fast as you, so sprinting never leaves them behind. Report a bug sends your report from inside the game and thanks you; nothing opens in another window. On computers every menu window has its own X in its corner. Vorthax has a new, more detailed look.

The crafting window tells you where you are: Workbench (warm wood), Furnace (grey stone), Workbench and Furnace, or plain Crafting. Near your chests a Stack button under Near and Hide puts your bag items into the chests that already hold them, and long chest names fit. A grappling hook falls when the block it holds breaks. Farmers only gather plants you have found, every crop grows wild somewhere, woodcutters replant what they cut, and saplings grow into trees two mornings later. Woodcutters and gathering pets bring half as much.

Pin any recipe to your checklist with the Checklist button beside Pin; tap it there when you stand by the right station to craft it (a warship at the workbench). The castle has soldier posts beside its arrow slits: press F on a tower floor, or use Buildings, to place archers there. Enemies outside can shoot back through a slit, but the stone around it stops about half of those shots. Your castle and buildings have more torches, evenly spaced on every floor. A villager works again as soon as their job block is within 15 blocks, keeps using it however far they go, and brings one along when they move into a new home; several can share a block. Workers wait for their foreman, a wanderer arrives on about one morning in five (never more than five days apart), and shop houses always match the castle's stage.

New in Beta 0.9.136

Getting ready for Steam: the Steam copy of the game earns Steam achievements for growing your village, taming, conquering and every boss, keeps your worlds in the Steam Cloud, and opens the Steam overlay. Steam keeps it up to date by itself.

New in Beta 0.9.135

The throne guards of the sky castle and the magma keep stand on the gold steps around the throne instead of being stuck inside them, so a throne room can be cleared by fighting. Any enemy that would start inside a wall steps out into the open.

New in Beta 0.9.134

Building next to your village no longer lifts or lowers the ground between the houses that are already there: only the gap beside the new building is levelled to meet it.

In a new world the fishing village never stands where the goblins put up their wooden lookout tower.

New in Beta 0.9.133

Beastmasters can tame cave creatures (bats, crabs, spiders, serpents, golems, cave bears and more) with 3 food: they follow you and fight at your side. They can tame bees too: a tamed bee buzzes around you and stings the next enemy with poison, then dies. In the Army window every tamed animal and creature has Release and Slaughter (tap twice).

Your castle keeps its notice board, chest, weapon rack and feed trough: if one goes missing (the Quartermaster's repairs used to cover them), it is put back, so the recruiter keeps working.

Emeralds, sapphires, rubies, amethysts and diamonds leave a dark wall of their own colour when you mine them, instead of the red stone or blue crystal wall.

Chests, workbenches, furnaces, tables, beds and other floor pieces fall when you mine the block under them (either half of a wide one); what a chest held spills onto the ground.

Miners come back to the foreman's hut every 30 seconds with what they dug, so none stays stuck down the mine. Tap a gold "Ready!" checklist to do it: place the building, grow the village (at your castle) or upgrade the shop; a villager's favor is handed over first when you carry it.

Animals no longer stay stuck inside blocks: one caught under a new building or walled in underground steps out to the nearest open spot.

While you aim with a block, back wall, plant, torch, furniture piece or door in hand, a faint picture of it shows where it will go. A door shows over both its cells, where it will really stand.

Woodcutters put logs in the lodge chest every morning, even on a day they felled nothing, and they look for trees all over your home island.

The goblins stay on their island: an enemy faction that takes the goblin forest no longer wipes out the goblin camps, and sleeping in a bed no longer sends the camps and the Beastmaster away. The Beastmaster and his bear come back to their camp three days after you beat him.

Every door places, stone and iron too: standing in the doorway (you step aside), with soldiers, villagers or animals there (they step out), under grass or snow, or aimed at the top half. Aim a door at an old door to swap them. If a door cannot go down, a message says why. A door you choose keeps its kind when the building around it turns to stone or iron.

The soldier posts window no longer opens by itself when you walk into a tower: press F inside and pick Place soldiers here (or use the building in the Buildings window).

The Small tower and the Stone watchtower have a hatch three platforms wide at the top, so you can jump up onto the roof easily. Towers you built before are widened too.

Exact (the aim button by the hotbar) mines the very block under your mouse. Under it, Hide keeps your soldiers and pets out of sight while you build (they still follow you). Chests can be named: type in the box at the top of the chest window.

Chests within 15 blocks help out: while the crafting or furnace window is open, what is in them counts as yours, and crafting takes from your bag first, then from them. The bag has a Stack to nearby chests button that puts your items into the chests that already hold them (your hotbar stays).

The crafting window follows the station you stand by: at a furnace you see only what the furnace makes; at a workbench its recipes and the by-hand ones; stand by both and everything is in one window. The Craft, ×5 and Max panel stays in view as you scroll down the list.

The grappling hook never lifts you through a roof: you climb onto a ledge only from beside it.

While the grappling hook holds you, you can still mine, fight, place blocks and use items. Press the hook key (E) again to fire a new hook where you aim and swing to the next hold; jump to let go.

Chests, workbenches, workshops and furnaces need flat, solid ground (or a platform, or another chest) under both halves. They no longer hang over a slope, a half block or empty air.

Tab opens the bag and E fires the grappling hook (it was X), so the hook sits right by your movement keys. If you kept the old keys, they switch over by themselves; keys you picked yourself stay as they are.

Saplings are planted in dirt: grass, dirt, farmland, sand or snow. They no longer go on stone or other hard blocks, where they never grew. Mushroom spores still go on cave stone.

Beta 0.9.132

A dash with the Fleetfoot sash or the Shadow cloak kicks up a small cloud of dust at your feet that drifts away behind you.

Beta 0.9.131

A thin strip of water three blocks wide dries up like any other thin puddle, instead of staying for good.

Beta 0.9.130

The Scaleborn's wings beat half as fast when he flies.

Beta 0.9.129

Marble pockets underground stay as dark as the rock around them; they no longer glow as if lit.

Beta 0.9.128

The Scaleborn is a red dragon-man: a horned dragon head with a long snout and a golden slit eye, scales with pale belly plates, tall bat wings and a thick spiked tail. Armour shows as shoulder guards, and a sash keeps your faction colour.

Beta 0.9.127

Cut a tree at any trunk block and the whole tree falls from the ground, bottom block included. A bee hive left hanging from nothing, under the leaves of a felled tree or below a block you broke, drops as an item, with 2 honey when it was full.

Beta 0.9.126

Enemies never appear within 10 blocks of you or a friend, and on a friend's screen far enemies no longer blink away and pop back. A soldier who falls 15 blocks behind joins you again even while you can see him; only while you are up inside a building does he wait below.

Beta 0.9.125

The hills, trees and mountains in the distance stand on the ground you can see, so they stay in view above the earth on high land and on hilltops, and the clouds rise with them when you go a little underground.

Beta 0.9.124

Your soldiers no longer pop onto you inside a tower: while you are up in a building they wait below or climb after you. When you walk away from a fight, travel by map, portal or mirror, or come back to life, your army stops chasing its old enemies and follows you again.

Beta 0.9.123

A grappling hook that catches while you fall cancels the fall damage, the way a double jump does: land after a catch and you are unhurt.

Beta 0.9.122

Enemies walk, they do not teleport: a raider on a village roof steps down to the nearest open ground instead of reappearing outside the village, a war party that gets stuck in view jumps instead of hopping forward, and on a friend's screen enemies are pulled back into place instead of snapping.

Beta 0.9.121

A quarter more gold ore and diamond ore, in new worlds and in rock nobody has dug yet.

Beta 0.9.120

Fewer one-block-high tunnels: most crawlways are two or three blocks high, in new worlds and in caves nobody has been to.

Beta 0.9.119

The back wall behind a rock is that rock's own wall: red stone, jade, rose and azure stone, granite, sandstone and the magma rocks each leave their own wall when broken instead of a crystal one.

Beta 0.9.118

Talk to the Head farmer to choose what each farmer gathers: crops from the field, or berries, insects, glowcaps, herbs, apples or honey picked around the farmhouse, with a few more of it in the chest each morning. The farmhouse chest opens from the same screen.

Beta 0.9.117

Raiders marching on your village now come by sea and land at the water's edge on the east or west side of your island. You are told which side when they set out and when they land, and a red arrow at that edge of the screen points at them while they are out of view.

Beta 0.9.116

Farmers cut the ripe crops in the farmhouse field and in every farm you built, and each morning the ripe plants are brought in before the day's share.

Beta 0.9.115

In a shared world, the small ledges you hop up inside a friend's watchtower now reach every player. Towers, keeps and small towers carry a flag in the builder's colour with the builder's name over it.

Beta 0.9.114

Farmers bring you the crops they grow. A harvest goes into the farmhouse chest as that crop (tomatoes, corn, melons and the rest, with a seed or two), empty furrows are sown from the seeds in the farmhouse chest first, and each morning every farmer puts a few of the field's own crops into the chest beside the grow meal.

Beta 0.9.113

Controller support is off for now.

Beta 0.9.112

The Near / Exact button sits to the right of the hotbar. Animals spawn on the ground, never inside a hill. Miners always get down the mine: the shaft is kept open (platforms on the ledges, nothing solid between), a miner starting a trip sinks straight down it to the floor, and whatever is left of a miner's daily quota at the end of the day is put into the miners' chest anyway.

Beta 0.9.111

On computers every menu window can be moved by the bar at its top and resized by its bottom-right corner, and the game remembers where you put it. Settings > Computer chooses where the bag and the crafting window open (left, centre or right), or puts crafting in the bag's window so you craft and sort in one place. "Put every window back" undoes it all.

Beta 0.9.110

The 1 to 9 keys pick a hotbar slot while the bag, crafting, a chest, a shop, the army, the map or the God menu is open, unless you are typing in a search box. Tapping another menu's button while one is open switches straight to it.

Beta 0.9.109

The log wall is a back wall: it goes behind you like the plank and stone walls (4 from a log; the solid log walls of the orc huts stay as they are). A small Near / Exact button sits beside the hotbar: Near mines the nearest block in the direction you aim or tap, Exact only the block you point at, and it works with a mouse too.

Beta 0.9.108

On computers the crafting panel opens on the left, where the bag opens, instead of at the right edge. Underground, every cave biome holds the same share of coal, iron, silver, gold and gems as the plain caves (the jade, rose, azure, dripstone, fossil, overgrown and mossy caves had about half); the gem caves keep their extra gems. Old worlds get the extra ore where you have not been. Bats, rose wisps, glow moths, wraiths and vultures fly: they cruise a few blocks over the ground instead of sliding along it, and dive or hang back to shoot. Swapping a block for the one in your hand takes a short hold on it, with a gold bar filling along the block, so a stray tap never eats a wall. The music is softer: no buzzing square waves, and fights play lower and slower.

Beta 0.9.107

The New world screen has a starting kit with both a recall mirror and a grappling hook ("+ Mirror and hook"), beside the mirror-only and hook-only kits. A hero you made earlier gets the kit's items as well.

Beta 0.9.106

The magma realm is mostly dark scoria and basalt now, with obsidian pockets and glowing ember stone; red magma rock only turns up in small pockets. The glow on magma rock and ember stone is little specks instead of lines. Adamant veins grow in any of the realm's rocks. Old worlds get the change where you have not been. The fog in the castle rooms you have not entered is loose and wispy: it drifts, flows across the room and spills a little past the walls, and it still clears room by room as you step in. The magma plants blend into the realm: dark stems and leaves in its own browns and reds with a spark of colour at the tips, much less glow, and they grow in patches.

Beta 0.9.105

The orc island's music no longer thuds like a drum every half second; that beat sounded like something being hit over and over. The tune itself stays.

Beta 0.9.104

The magma realm has more kinds of rock: obsidian pockets, bands of basalt (also hanging from cavern ceilings), ember stone with glowing cracks, crumbly scoria, and magma dirt on the open floors, where the magma plants grow; the red magma rock is only part of it. Old worlds get this where you have not been yet. The Sky Ranger's tower is twice as wide with taller floors and a throne hall twice as high; the Magma Knight's maze is twice as wide with taller halls and a throne room twice as wide. Old worlds get the bigger castles rebuilt where they stand, with their lords and guards. Rooms you have not entered are hidden by thick drifting smoke, white in the tower and red in the maze, that clears room by room as you step in.

Beta 0.9.103

Lava burns through every plant, sapling, glow plant, cobweb and rug that water flows through, instead of stopping at them; it still stops at chests, doors and furniture, hardens on water and hurts as before. The antler rod has a white antler shaft. The bug net's rim sits across the end of the shaft and the mesh runs forward to a tip at the top.

Beta 0.9.102

Crystal golems take the colour of their caves: jade green, rose pink, azure blue, white quartz in dripstone caves, amber in root caves, ivory in fossil caves, moss green-gold in the overgrown caverns, and sapphire, emerald or ruby in the gem caves.

Beta 0.9.101

The bug net catches every insect in the path of your swing (about 3 blocks ahead, 2.5 up and down, or within 2 blocks of where you aim), counting each insect's body rather than a single point, so a near miss still catches. The net looks like a net: the handle meets the rim at its widest, and the mesh hangs down to a point. A caught insect chirps, and a killed one pops.

Beta 0.9.100

Insects on the hook lure better catches: the catch is rolled twice and you get the better one, and the insect is kept after a catch about a third of the time. The sky realm has cloud moths, sky skimmers and sun beetles, and the magma realm ember moths, cinder beetles and ash wasps: they bring up the best fish and treasure. Each cave biome has its own insect: jade weevils, rose moths, azure midges, drip mites, root crickets, bone beetles and lantern flies. More animals roam the land. About half of the deer are bucks with big antlers; bucks in a pen shed antlers into the trough chest and hunted bucks drop them, and two antlers make the antler rod (as good as gold; insects on it bite sooner and are kept 70% of the time). A full-strength cast lands on the farthest water within reach and stays on the line.

Beta 0.9.99

Bee hives hang under the leaves of trees near flowers, and you can build one at a workbench (8 planks and a jar of honey) and hang it under any block. Bees fly between the flowers and their hive. A hive with flowers within 12 blocks fills with honey each morning and drips when it is full: tap it to take two jars. Butterflies come in ten colours and beetles in eight. The bug net swings like a pickaxe while you hold the button.

Beta 0.9.98

Insects die from one hit of any sword, pickaxe, axe, hoe, hammer or rod: every insect in the path of your swing (about 3 blocks ahead of you, a little behind, and 2 blocks around where you aim) is killed at once. Only the bug net catches them alive.

Beta 0.9.97

Insects live around you: butterflies and bees by flowers, dragonflies over water, fireflies over the grass at night, crickets in tall grass, beetles in the woods and in caves, sand fleas on the beach and glow flies by glowing mushrooms underground. Catch them alive with a bug net (3 sticks and 2 wool at a workbench, or from the Fisher): swing it at one and it goes in your bag. Swing anything else at an insect, or shoot it, and it dies and leaves nothing. Every insect is fishing bait. Cutting tall grass, digging beach sand or breaking a glowing mushroom can startle one out for you to net.

Beta 0.9.96

Placing a building takes two taps or clicks: the first shows a box where it would go, green when it fits and red when something is in the way, and a second tap inside the green box builds it there (tap anywhere else to move the box). Building spots follow the older rule again: trees, grass and plants are cleared, along with mist clouds, bushes, ivy and hanging moss, but bumps of ground are no longer dug away. The animal pen is a whole barn: plank walls with a door at each end, a roof, a loft and a trough chest, and your penned animals live inside.

Beta 0.9.95

A building whose base is blown away crumbles straight down where it stood instead of tipping over: its blocks break apart and fall in a cloud of dust, and it lands as a heap of crumbled back walls.

Beta 0.9.94

Your war machines hold their ground: when an enemy comes in range they stay where they are and fire, and they reach farther (ballista 34 blocks, cannon 28, trebuchet 50). They follow you again a few seconds after the fight, without shuffling or hopping. Enemy armies fight in formation when they are three or more with two kinds of soldier: their toughest melee in the front rank (bracing against your blows), the rest in ranks behind, and their archers and mages behind the melee.

Beta 0.9.93

Buildings go up where the ground is clear: drifting mist, bushes and flowers are cleared away (tall towers used to be refused by the mist above them). On a phone, Cancel is a small button at the bottom of the screen while you place a building. Bombs, cannonballs and trebuchet boulders also break the back walls in the space they blow open: dirt, stone, wood and the rest. In the test world, the God menu's World tab sets the day and the time, claims the village at once, and sets off an enemy raid, a siege army (and brings it straight to your village), a dragon raid, enemy war machines, a monster wave, or damage to your village to try the repairs.

Beta 0.9.92

When the enemy damages your village (cannons, trebuchets, bombs, fire), talk to your Quartermaster: he offers to repair it and puts every broken block back over part of a day, faster while you sleep. When you beat an enemy faction, its last soldiers surrender and join you straight away. Its own helpers leave and a new Quartermaster arrives at its castle: talk to him to fix up the castle and claim it, putting back what the battle broke, and a Recruiter and a Beast trainer move in. If any of them is lost, a new one comes.

Beta 0.9.91

Enemy siege engines break the walls of your village: houses, shops and the castle walls can be holed by cannonballs and trebuchet boulders, and a house whose base is blown away falls down. The castle never falls down whole, and chests keep their contents. Your own bombs still never harm your village. Rebuild what they break, or stop the engines before they fire.

Beta 0.9.90

War machines miss sometimes: a ballista hits about three shots in four, a cannon three in five, a trebuchet one in two (a little better when you work it yourself), and a miss lands a few blocks wide. Their blasts are bigger, with smaller bursts around the main one, more smoke, and battle smoke lasts half as long again. Cannonballs and boulders leave scorched ground around the crater, like bombs. Blow away the base of a building with bombs or war machines and it comes down: a tall tower topples over like a tree, a house drops onto its ruins, and what falls becomes crumbled back walls instead of dropping blocks (anything in a chest spills out). Castles and your own village never fall.

Beta 0.9.89

Siege armies: from day 15, every 5 days one enemy faction sends a bigger army against your village with a cannon and a ballista, and from day 20 a trebuchet too. Their engines set up outside your walls with archer crews; kill the crews or wreck the engines. Scouts warn you the evening before. Siege fire hurts anyone in your village but breaks none of its blocks. Ordinary raids still come on other days (from day 5, about one morning in five) and from day 15 bring a ballista. Cannonballs and trebuchet boulders burst in a fireball with a shock ring, flying debris and smoke, and nearby blasts shake the screen.

Beta 0.9.88

War machines: trebuchet boulders hit much harder, crash through tree crowns into the ground beneath, and land where you aim; ballista bolts fly true. With the right stick, how far you push it sets how far the shot goes, and a crosshair shows where it will land. A Step off button sits at the top of the screen while you work a machine. With crewed machines, a Machines button under the move stick marks one target for all of them (hold it to let them choose again). Machines keep back from the fighting, follow you twice as far before catching up, ride on any boat, and can be packed into your bag. From day 15, enemy attacks on your village can bring a ballista; you are warned from day 10.

Fishing: the storm rod (a mythril rod and storm bars) only bites in a storm, and brings up storm fish no other rod can catch, now and then even a Kraken lure. Bait makes fish bite sooner: worms from digging, grubs from logs, crickets from tall grass, sand fleas from beach sand and glow flies from glowing mushrooms. Team charms (war, swift, shield and mending banners) lift everyone on your side near you. Six new crops (tomatoes, corn, strawberries, onions, cabbage and melons) grow wild and on tilled soil, feed and tame animals, and cook into new meals. The Buildings window has a Farmhouse with a ready field, and the animal pen has taller fences, a gate, a rail and a trough.

Beta 0.9.87

Vorthax follows you: once you have stepped into its lair it is awake, and if you leave it bursts out after you and fights you in the open, where your whole army can reach it. It gives up and flies home if you get far away, go up to the sky or down to the magma realm, or stay out of its reach for about half a minute. The wiki lists the army each boss needs, a suggested size and a good mix of soldiers. Pickaxe icons have no gaps, hammer heads are angled to strike to the right, and axe heads are turned so the blade points straight out from the handle.

Beta 0.9.86

A desert: one wild island is all sand and sandstone, with cacti, sand cave walls down to the shale, and five creatures of its own: dune scorpions, jackal packs and vultures by day, mummies and sand wraiths at night and in the sand caves. Sand falls when nothing holds it up, and it hurts whoever is under it; sandstone stays put.

The magma realm is wide open with a black void behind it, its floors glow with blaze lilies, sulfur puffs and flame grass, and magma salamanders, ash wraiths and obsidian beetles hunt there. Wizards' staffs hit 30% harder and every bolt flies on through a second enemy. A Cancel building button sits at the top of the screen while you choose where to build. The fishing village never lands on an orc island or beside a camp, ruin or tower, and the Goblin Beastmaster always keeps his scarred bear.

Beta 0.9.85

Rainy days look it: the sky and clouds turn grey and the day grows a little darker, more so in a storm. Camps on the surface hold orcs or goblins instead of zombies and skeletons; snowy islands keep their frost folk.

Formations: the old orders are gone. Your soldiers always follow you and fight what comes near; while you move they run with you, and when you stop they step into their places and hold them. Pick a formation in the Army window (knights first, maces first, beasts first, wizards close or archers forward) and where you stand: at the front, in the middle or at the back. A small picture there shows the line. Q changes the formation. Enemy archers and wizards keep behind their own front line too.

Enemy towers: clear every guard from a watchtower, outpost or keep, stand close, and you choose whether to capture it. Placing soldiers is done on a picture of the building: tap a soldier, then a glowing post. Walking into one of your towers with empty posts opens it for you; a checkbox there turns that off. The world name box is the first thing on the New world screen.

Beta 0.9.84

Save as file in the Report a bug screen works on the claude.ai page: the page asks you before it saves the report.

Beta 0.9.83

Cobwebs catch you: walk into one and you crawl and sink through it slowly, then tear free after a moment; a tap tears a web at once, with anything in hand. Enemies get caught too. Vines hang as one plant when they grow in a chain, you climb them like a ladder (up to climb, down to slide, let go to hang), and there are many more of them under cave ceilings and overhangs. The abandoned village stands up to its back walls: where a back wall remains, the house's side walls stand with it, ragged at the top, and the stone, brick, planks and back walls are cracked, crumbled and mossy. When the repairs are done a small note asks you back to the castle to choose the villagers' jobs. From inside a building you still see the rain outside. On computers the crafting menu opens at the right side of the screen and the bag at the left. There is half again as much coal and a quarter more iron and silver, mostly in the rock near the surface. Gold is a little rarer. The castle's upper floor is one room. Crafting shows what you can make where you stand: walk from the furnace to a workbench and the recipes follow. Open doors pass in front of you. Enemy scouts come into the caves only under their own island. Torches sit on slopes. Chests have a Sort button and an X. Stuck workers find their way home with what they carry. A tree struck by lightning leaves a charred silhouette behind its burnt pieces. Emptied goblin and orc camps fill up again after three days. Snow islands are snow and ice down to the shale, with snow cave walls and a Snow wall you can craft. At most three fighters stand on one block. Buildings stand on solid ground. Report a bug from the pause menu or the title screen: it sends the version, your world and the last errors to the developers' bug list.

Beta 0.9.82

Fixes from playtesting: digging no longer turns the screen bright (a swing left the picture in the wrong place), and when you play with friends the host's block changes reach them in the order they happened, so nobody ends up with the old block. Save and quit to title ends the multiplayer game, so you can host the saved world again straight away, and a friend who quits can start a world of their own. A friend alone at an enemy village meets the same closed ranks as the host: bring soldiers. A double-click on a shop row buys that item once. A shop house upgraded under a hill or another building keeps its low roof and tells you; clear the space above it and the upper floor is built. Seeds go into the soil right under your feet, or under a soldier standing beside you, the moment you click. A torch placed on a fence sits on the post and is drawn in front of you. Cobwebs in ruins come in six shapes: top corners, bottom corners, hanging from ceilings and on bare walls. A sapling only grows into the room it has. Diamonds are found only in chests of the deepstone layer and below, one or two at a time; there is a quarter more iron and silver in small pockets. On computers the bag opens as a panel under the hotbar (click the world to close it) and crafting shows the categories in a column on the left with group headings that stay while you scroll and a Top button. The Multiplayer menu has a Copy bug report button that copies the connection details and recent events as text, to paste into a message.

Beta 0.9.81

Playing together: your own game runs the enemies near you, so they chase, turn and strike on your screen at once, and the host only corrects them when the two games drift apart. An enemy that reaches you hurts you right away; the number you see when you hit one is the number that counts. Bosses, the dragon and animals still follow the host. Less is sent over the network too. Mining looks calmer: the body stays still and only the arm and the tool move. Swings start at the shoulder and shots leave the hand instead of the middle of the body.

Beta 0.9.80

Playing in a friend's world, an enemy you finish off dies on the spot instead of a moment later when the host confirms it (the loot still comes from the host right after). Every world you join is kept under Continue with its code, so you can open any of them again, not only the last one. On a computer the option box for a furnace, a villager or an animal sits centred above what they say; on a phone it stays where it was and their words move up above it.

Beta 0.9.79

Your hero works with the whole body: the arm reaches along the swing of a pick, axe, hoe or hammer with the tool in the hand, the body leans into each stroke, and placing a block reaches toward the spot with the block in hand. While the Quartermaster fixes up the village, sleeping moves the repairs along by the hours you slept, and he is the only villager there until the work is done: the Beast trainer, the Recruiter and any wanderer arrive when it is finished. The ruin looks the part before that: cobwebs in the corners and under the ceilings, crumbled stone and brick where the walls fell, broken planks and rubble on the floors. Water: sloped and stepped blocks beside water show the water in their open part; a puddle of one or two eighths standing alone, or water spread into a thin film over flat ground, dries up; a chest under water no longer pokes its lid through the water above it.

Beta 0.9.78

Water was checked against every block. Saplings and spores, cactus, sugar cane, the glowing cave plants, the giant grove plants, wall shards, banners, paintings and rugs are covered by water and come back when it drains, instead of holding it back or being lost. Crystal blocks no longer let water through. A bucket poured onto a plant covers it instead of breaking it. A grass block with a solid block on top turns to plain dirt. A sapling only goes on an empty cell: it never replaces a plant, a crop or anything else.

Beta 0.9.77

Eight more cave creatures, each at home in one kind of cave: dripstone golems in the stalagmite caves, root wyrms in the root caverns, jade mantises in the jade caves, rose serpents in the rose caves, bone hounds in the fossil beds, shale crawlers in the shale layer, deep stalkers in the deepstone layer and moss trolls in the moss caves. Goblins, zombies, skeletons and orcs now only roam the top quarter of the underground; deeper down, every creature belongs to the cave it lives in. A chest, shelf, barrel, cupboard or desk with anything in it can no longer be broken by any means (empty it first), and tapping a barrel, cupboard, desk or shelf opens it just like a chest.

Beta 0.9.76

The abandoned village is a two-storey castle and three houses left to the weather: ragged gaps in the walls, moss over the stonework, grass, ferns and saplings on the floors, vines and ivy on the walls. The Quartermaster waits inside. Walking in no longer claims the village: talk to him and choose "Fix up the castle and the houses", and the repairs run over about a day, block by block from the ground up; the Beast trainer and the Recruiter arrive when he starts, and the drifters pick their jobs when the work is done. Burned villages are built around the fire that took each house: the roof and one upper corner are gone with ragged edges, nothing floats, wood near the fire is charred, the back walls are charred with holes where the fire burned through, and grass, ferns, bushes and saplings grow through the ash. Older worlds get the new look where nobody has explored yet.

Beta 0.9.75

The overgrown caverns are a deeper, darker green, with glow vines hanging from the roofs and spores drifting through the air. Cave and tunnel walls vary: cobbled, cracked and mossy patches among the plain rock. Every chest in the world stands on two solid blocks, loose rock floating in caves is cleared, and sealed one-block pockets in the rock are filled, so caves read as one connected mass. Older worlds get the walls, supports and tidy-up in ground you have not explored yet.

Beta 0.9.74

Ore veins take on the rock around them: iron in the jade caves is green jade stone with iron flecks, in the shale layer it is shale with iron flecks, so caves keep their colour and you can still spot the ore. Every cave biome grows its own glowing mushroom and glowing plant (jade glowcaps and ferns, rose glowcaps and lilies, azure glowcaps and frost bells, amber glowcaps and reeds, ember glowcaps and lantern flowers, bone glowcaps and ghost orchids); break them to take them home as lights. Deep in the shale layer lie the overgrown caverns: giant glowcaps and ferns you can stand on, giant glowing blooms, hanging moss and glowing moss underfoot. Giant cave spiders, cave bears, thornback beetles and glow moths live there and hit harder than anything else in the caves, but the caverns hide gold caches with crystals, gems, gold bars and extra coins. Older worlds get the plants and the caverns in ground you have not explored yet.

Beta 0.9.73

The wiki's Biomes and places page has a picture of every place in the game, from the ice islands to the fossil beds, and wiki pages open faster. The shale layer has its own back wall; in 0.9.72 it borrowed the jade caves' wall.

Beta 0.9.72

Three rock layers: stone near the surface, then shale (a layered purple-grey rock) from about a third of the way down, then deepstone from a little over halfway to the magma realm. Older worlds get the shale layer in ground you have not explored yet. Gear (weapons, armor, accessories, charms, tools and hooks) is found only in cave chests at or below the shale layer; cave chests above it hold ore, potions, food, torches and a few more coins. Chests in ruins, war camps, castles, the dragon's lair and the orc cave are as they were. Every chest in the world is filled once and never refills.

Beta 0.9.71

Shared worlds: every change to the world travels one way, in order, so a friend's block can no longer be undone by an older message, and each message is about 800 bytes lighter. A friend whose game fell behind the host's changes (a long pause, a hidden tab) gets a fresh copy of the world instead of a world with holes, and stays where they were.

Beta 0.9.70

One dragon, one Kraken: in a shared world the host runs Vorthax and the Kraken for everyone, like every other enemy, so all players see the same fight in the same place. They fight whichever player is nearest, so a friend alone in the lair or out at sea gets the full fight, and a friend's hits land through the host.

Beta 0.9.69

Chests in shared worlds: two players can use the same chest at the same time and nothing is lost or doubled. The host keeps every chest; a friend's change goes to the host as "took 5 iron from slot 3, put 7 apples", the host applies it and answers. If someone else took the same item first, it comes back out of your bag with a note. What your woodcutters, farmers and miners deliver now shows for friends right away, without the host opening the chest. When a lot is happening, the host's messages keep the enemies and the world and drop the effects first.

Beta 0.9.68

Cover and bracing are for battles between the three factions: you, your soldiers and the enemy factions' soldiers. The guards of the wizard towers and the sky and magma castles don't take cover behind walls or brace in a line.

Beta 0.9.67

Sturdier shared worlds: when the host switches to another app or tab, their world keeps running for everyone, so friends are no longer left waiting or dropped. A friend's game no longer runs enemy village guards, scouting parties, sky knights or enemy village growth on its own (the host runs them for everyone), and the numbers that tell enemies and animals apart carry on when the host starts the world again, so a friend's tamed animals never get mixed up with new ones.

Beta 0.9.66

A deeper underground: new worlds go twice as deep below the islands, and the sea floor still reaches all the way down to the magma realm. The lowest caves, just above the magma realm, are winding tunnels with pockets of lava instead of one huge open cavern. Cave floors have rounded edges like the hills, and underground pools of water and lava are rounded bowls with ragged rims and air pockets instead of boxes. Older worlds get the tunnels, the lava pockets, the rounded edges and the rounded pools wherever nobody has explored yet. Saved worlds now go to the browser's larger storage, so bigger worlds and more of them fit.

Beta 0.9.65

Smoother shared worlds: a friend in your world sees enemies and animals glide smoothly instead of jumping, even on a slow connection. Their hits show at once (the number, the sound and the push) and the host applies them with the weapon's own knockback, kills vanish as soon as the host confirms them, every enemy hit reaches them, and their game knows which enemies are after them.

Workplaces level up: the woodcutter's lodge, the farmhouse and the miners' hut go from level 1 to 3 like every shop (Buildings, Village). The head worker asks a favor first. Each level makes room for 2 more workers and they bring in more, level 2 adds a loft with a bed and level 3 lanterns, a chimney and a banner. Five new cave monsters: cave bats in every cave (swarms in the dripstone caves), armored jade crabs, glowing rose wisps that throw bolts, azure spiders whose bite slows you, and fossil raptors that pounce in packs. More monsters lurk underground.

Formations: give your party the Formation order (in the Army window, or press Q until it says Formation). Your soldiers line up in ranks facing the nearest enemy, three to a block: the toughest melee soldiers in front, the next rank right behind them striking over their shoulders with longer reach, and archers and wizards behind you. The line holds its ground instead of chasing, and the front rank braces, taking less damage and knockback from the front. Any soldier, yours or an enemy's, standing shoulder to shoulder with two others braces the same way, so a packed enemy line is harder to break. Cover: a block or a door beside you, on the side a shot comes from, turns some shots aside (about a third with a low wall, more than half with full cover), and archers and wizards prefer targets standing in the open.

Beta 0.9.64

Favors before upgrades: before a shopkeeper upgrades their shop, they ask you for something from their own trade. The blacksmith wants ore or diamonds, the cook wants meat, eggs or honey, the fisher wants fish, the shipwright wants logs or pearls, and so on. What they ask for changes from world to world. Bring it, tap Give in their shop, and the upgrade opens. Growing your village works the same way: the quartermaster asks for supplies first (Buildings, Village). The Jeweler moves in once your village is a Town and the Archmage is beaten, and the War engineer once it is a City and you have taken an enemy castle. Rooms are lit by torches and lamps: a closed room with no torch is dim even at midday, and only windows and openings let daylight in. Every room your village built gets a torch once.

Beta 0.9.63

Trap doors: doors that lie in the floor, made at a workbench from any wood's planks, castle stone, deep stone brick or iron bars. Closed, you stand on one and nothing comes up through it. Tap it to open or shut it, jump up under it, or hold down while standing on it; it opens for you and shuts as soon as you are through. Your soldiers and tamed animals can follow you through, but enemies never open one. In your castle, the ledges up from the great hall end in trap doors that match the castle's stone, deep stone or iron, and the upper floor's west doorway has a door where a bed used to stand, so the upper floor is sealed off as your safe room.

Beta 0.9.62

Gem weapons: at a workbench, the Iron, Gold and Diamond weapon of a kind (Silver, Gold and Diamond for staffs) plus 4 gems make a special one, and the gem decides what it does. Bows and staffs: ruby burns (Fire bow, Ember staff), sapphire splits arrows or chains lightning (Tri-shot bow, Tempest staff), emerald blasts or wards (Blast bow, Ward staff), amethyst pierces every enemy in its path (Void bow, Void staff). Knights, macebearers and Beastmasters get thrown weapons, a glaive, flail or kunai for each gem: ruby burns, sapphire chills, emerald heals you a little each hit, amethyst flies farther and knocks back harder. No weapon you can have before the diamond tier beats a Diamond weapon. Grow meal (from bones, or seeds, glowcaps and berries at a composter, and left by your farmers each morning) grows a crop a stage or a sapling into a tree. Beat both wizards to unlock the Breakdown bench: next to it, any crafted item in your bag breaks back into all its materials. Your castle's arrow slits turn dark slate and then iron as it grows, nothing spawns on top of your buildings, and the chimney on a level 2 shop house sits on its roof.

Beta 0.9.61

Rugs lie flat on the floor, covering the top of the block they sit on, and come in six kinds: wool, blue, green, golden, striped and a bamboo mat. Jade, rose quartz and azure crystals hang from ceilings and grow out of cave walls like amethyst, and mining the block that holds a crystal knocks it loose. Enemies take fall damage. Accessories and charms turn up in chests half as often. Bows and staffs say their material: Wooden bow, Iron bow, Wooden staff, Gold staff. Settings, Screen layout has sliders for the checklist, the menu icons and the action buttons, and the choice list that opens with F has the X too.

Beta 0.9.60

Lava lies only underground, in puddles, pools and lakes of many sizes, each a bowl with air above it; lava that sat on the surface in older worlds has cooled to stone. Friends who join a shared world can tame the host's animals (they become the friend's own pets and the host's wild one goes away) and feed them for breeding, and a friend's game no longer makes stray enemies or animals of its own that the host never sees.

Beta 0.9.59

The wood of medium and tall trees stays behind the leaves: their wide trunks no longer show through the crown. The ground under houses, lodges, the castle and every building you place stays flat, with no slanted blocks below them. Lava sets you on fire (a cooling band or better ward stops it), and animals that wander into lava burn and die. A new world starts without the buildings of the world you played before.

Beta 0.9.58

Rain never builds up: it leaves no puddles and brings no floods at any weather strength, and the weather choices on the New world screen say so. Any old rainwater still lying in an older world dries up the next morning.

Beta 0.9.57

Bombs throw up much more smoke, and smoke hangs in the air longer (about 45 seconds); rain, storms and snow clear it from the open air two to five times faster. A ballista, cannon or trebuchet can only be set up when a free soldier in your party is with you, and that soldier works it. Press F beside a crewed machine (or use the Army window) and choose Aim, then click or tap a spot: the crew fires at enemies near the mark, or at the mark itself. "Own targets" lets it choose again. War machines are drawn at close to their real size next to you. In the test world a soldier joins you to work a machine if none is free.

Beta 0.9.56

Sugar bakes into sugar cake, berry tart, sugar cookies and candied apples at a furnace. Sea treasures make things: eight ancient coins and a gold bar make a Merchant's charm, an old compass becomes a Dragon compass or an Astrolabe, two golden fish with pearls make the Lucky lure (or roast one into a golden fish feast), a sunken crown with pearls becomes the Tidecrown charm (+20 health, +20 mana, faster mana), Kraken ink with a black pearl makes the Shadow cloak, and coral presses into pink coral blocks. The Sage charm's faster mana refill works.

Beta 0.9.55

Mana refills faster the more mana you have: a wizard gets back 12% of their maximum mana every second and everyone else 8% (never slower than before), so spirit gems and other mana upgrades also speed up the refill. Wizards start with 90 health. The Archmage tower has about half as many guards. Items that shared a name have their own now: the Kraken's treasure-chest daggers are Tidebond daggers, the chain-lightning staff is the Tempest staff, and the mushroom you eat is a Glowcap. Metal bars, gems, crystals, mana potions, farm goods and sea treasures all have descriptions.

Beta 0.9.54

The red faction's light roof tiles are a brighter red instead of pink.

Beta 0.9.53

When a boss falls in a shared world, every player gets their own copy of its loot; coins and everything else on the ground go to whoever picks them up first. Blasts, cannon shots and fires leave smoke that drifts up and fades over about 20 seconds and piles up in a big battle: it greys the view, and arrows and spells shot through it spread from 5% in a light haze up to 35% in thick smoke. Rain and storms still fall but leave no water on the ground and bring no floods, and fog days come in light, normal and thick. Days and nights last twice as long (10 minutes of day, 4 of night). The castle's whole second floor is the safe room. While you are away, your world keeps going (up to 3 days): crops grow, and woodcutters, farmers and miners bring in their work. Stone buildings have light roofs in your faction's colour. Underground there are jade, rose and azure caves with glowing crystals, stalagmite caves, root caverns with glow bulbs and fossil beds.

Beta 0.9.52

A grappling hook that has bitten holds a taut, straight line from your hand to the claw while it pulls you in and while you hang; the rope no longer folds over into a loop above you.

Beta 0.9.51

Paths run along the ground between the buildings of your village and grow with it: trampled dirt for a Hamlet, cobblestone for a Town and an iron walkway for a City. Enemy villages have them too. You can also make all three to lay your own: dirt path from dirt, cobblestone path from stone, iron walkway from iron and stone.

Beta 0.9.50

Houses no longer show a strip of sky behind the floor between their second and third storeys: every building fills small gaps in its back wall. The castle's halls keep the same light wherever you stand, lit by their torches and lanterns; an open door no longer floods a building with daylight.

Beta 0.9.49

Every villager needs a home with a bed, a chest and the item of their trade: an anvil for the blacksmith, a cooking pot for the cook, a herb rack, a barrel for the fisher, a gem bench, a ship's wheel, a drafting table, a powder keg, a weapon rack for the Quartermaster, a notice board, a feed trough, a composter for farmers, a chopping block for woodcutters and an ore cart for miners. Your village's buildings come furnished; if one of the three goes missing, that villager stops working until it is back. Build your own home anywhere near the village (a closed room with walls, floor, roof, back wall and a door, plus the three items) and a villager of that trade moves in; the Buildings window lists every home and lets you move villagers. A Guard post placed in any such home becomes a soldier post. Furniture comes in stone, deep stone and iron and changes with the building. Roofs are your faction's colour at the stone and iron stages, and enemy villages grow through the same stages in their own colours. Every building lays dirt under itself and levels the ground to its neighbours the same way.

Beta 0.9.48

Your castle starts as stone, turns to dark deep stone for a Town and iron for a City. Stone doors and iron doors can be crafted at the workbench, and village buildings use them at their stone and iron stages. Woodcutters, farmers and miners now start with a wanderer: give one the job and they become its head and build the lodge, farmhouse or mine; then the Quartermaster hires up to 5 of each for 50 coins. The miners' hut grows from wood to stone to iron with your village, and the mine shaft has a platform across its top. The top shop house keeps its red tile roof without the turrets, its back walls have no gaps, and its balcony lantern hangs under a little canopy. The lodge and farmhouse stand level with your village, and the ground between neighbouring buildings is flat, with a slope only past the last one. The small tower has nothing over its hatch, so you can jump up to the roof. In the test world every building and upgrade is free.

Beta 0.9.47

Crafting is a grid of pictures: things you can make right now light up and come first, and tapping one shows what it needs, what you have, where it is made and Craft, ×5 and Max buttons. Star a recipe with Pin to keep it at the top. More tabs split the long lists: Furniture, Lights and decor, Materials, Farm and animals, Boats and machines, Potions and runes. The chest window shows your bag on the left and the chest on the right, sized to fit the screen, with Take all first. A shop house at level 3 gets a red clay tile roof with a turret on each corner instead of gold trim.

Beta 0.9.46

The portal on top of the stone keep stands in the middle of the roof (keeps you already built move it there). The wiki shows every building in your village at each step: the castle as a Hamlet, a Town and a City, the village houses, a shop house at levels 1, 2 and 3, and the woodcutter's lodge and farmhouse, with what each upgrade costs.

Beta 0.9.45

Watchtowers, keeps and small towers have arrow slits on their roofs, so the soldiers posted up top shoot through them too; the watchtower has 6 posts (two on each upper floor and two on the roof). Each building in the Buildings window has its own picture, and the animal pen shows a fence with crops and a sheep. The wiki has a Buildings section: every building with its cost, size and a picture of each numbered soldier post.

Beta 0.9.44

Archers and mages posted in towers, keeps and on roofs see over the wall beside them, aim at enemies far below and reach a little farther, so they shoot at whatever comes at their side of the building. Raiders always arrive from outside your village: any enemy soldier found on a village roof is put back on open ground outside, and monsters never appear on your roofs. The battlement wall is a small tower: one room with a doorway on each side, arrow slits over the doors and a lookout roof (4 posts). The orc huts are built of solid log walls, not tree trunks you could walk through. Every wood has its own plank wall and its own furniture look: spruce grain, birch flecks, palm weave, jungle vines and dark oak gold studs, and furniture has a dark outline so it stands out against any wall. Barrels, cupboards and desks store items, and you can sit on chairs, benches and stools to heal three times as fast. The miners' chest opens like any other chest.

Beta 0.9.43

Watchtowers have no glass: the bottom room is solid wall over the doors, and every floor above has arrow slits where the guards stand, so they can shoot out. The top room of every tower, yours and every faction's, is 4 blocks tall. Keeps have slits upstairs and solid walls over their doors. Window walls are a back wall of glass panes (4 from 1 glass and 1 stick at a workbench): the sky shows through and daylight comes in. Every table, chair, bench, stool, bed, bookshelf, cupboard, desk, barrel and workbench comes in all six woods; oak pieces take any planks, the others take their own wood. Planks of every wood sell for the same, and so do logs. New saplings: a pine sapling (a spruce sapling and 2 snow) and blue, green, red and orange mushroom spores (from the caps of giant mushrooms) that grow giant mushrooms on stone, moss, dirt or grass. The Herbalist sells every sapling and spore.

Beta 0.9.42

Every building in your village follows the same wood, stone and iron steps as the castle: the huts, battlement walls, watchtowers, animal pens and keeps you build yourself, and the outposts and keeps you capture, are wood in a Hamlet, stone in a Town and iron in a City, together with the castle, the houses, the lodge and the farmhouse. Shop houses keep following their own shop level.

Beta 0.9.41

Your buildings show how far your village has come. As a Hamlet your castle, houses, woodcutter's lodge and farmhouse are wood: plank walls, timber beams and thatch roofs. Growing into a Town rebuilds them in stone with tiled roofs, and a City rebuilds them in riveted iron with iron roofs. Each shop's house follows its own shop level instead: wood at level 1, stone at level 2, iron at level 3. Wood can catch fire in raids and storms, stone cannot, and iron plate takes an iron pickaxe to break. Furniture, doors, windows and chests stay where they are. Thatch, iron plate, iron beams and iron roofs can be crafted at a workbench too.

Beta 0.9.40

Melee leaders lift the fighters around them. Every beastmaster, knight and macebearer, you or a soldier, helps everyone on their side within 8 blocks, themselves included: beastmasters make them 10% faster, knights make them take 15% less damage and macebearers make them hit 15% harder. One of each kind counts, and enemies get the same from their own leaders. The lifts you have show under your coins. Faction bonuses reach every soldier of that color: archers and wizards shoot faster and their arrows and bolts fly faster, and macebearers reach farther.

Beta 0.9.39

In a shared world every friend has a health bar over their head, under their name: a gold-framed bar with a heart that turns from green to yellow to red, and flashes when they are close to falling. Soldiers keep their thin red line, so friends are easy to tell apart.

Beta 0.9.38

Checklists: every building, growing the village and each shop upgrade has a Checklist button. It pins a small list to your screen showing how many of each item you have and need, with a check mark once you have enough. When everything is there the list glows "Ready!", and it goes away once you build or upgrade. You can pin up to 3, and choose where they sit and how big they are in Settings > Screen. The health, mana and hunger bars are bigger, with icons, notches every tenth, a pale trail that drains after a hit, and a flash when one runs low.

Beta 0.9.37

Bird cages work for everyone in a shared world: a friend can put a bird in any cage, every player sees the birds and the eggs they lay, and eggs one player collects are gone for the others.

Beta 0.9.36

New worlds: the wizard tower stands alone on a small island of its own. Caves are richer: big caverns have rock pillars with ore in them, ledges with hanging stone and boulders; winding tunnels run from narrow crawlways to wide galleries; and small buildings with chests hide beside the caves: miners' camps, stone shrines, deep vaults and crystal grottos with gold chests, and mushroom huts. Worlds you already have keep their caves and tower exactly as they are.

Beta 0.9.35

Grappling hooks fire straight where you aim the moment you press E (or let go of the Hook dial), bite the first wall, ceiling or ledge in their path and pull you there; each hook reaches farther (10, 16, 24 blocks) and has its own colors. New permanent accessories: a Bait pouch, Fisher's ring and Lucky lure for fishing; a Cooling band, Ward amulet and Dragon scale ward against burning, frost, knockback and lava; a Fleetfoot sash and Shadow cloak to dash by double-tapping left or right; the Swift and Windstep boots are back; and a Wayfinder stone opens the travel map anywhere with free trips. Some are sold by the Jeweler and Fisher, some are crafted, and the best drop from bosses. Beating the Goblin Beastmaster opens a portal at his war camp, and beating Grukk one in the middle of the orc island.

Beta 0.9.34

Animals: boars give boar meat and beavers beaver meat, and hawks, eagles, owls and penguins each have their own meat, raw and cooked. Pigs live in the grasslands (pork when hunted). Birds of every kind go in a bird cage (crafted at a workbench), never a fenced pen, and lay eggs there each morning; use the cage to collect them or let a bird out. As pets, only birds gather; other animals produce or collect food in a pen: cows milk, sheep wool, pigs mushrooms and carrots, boars grass and seeds, rabbits berries and carrots. Piglets, beaver kits and fluffy chicks of hawks, eagles and owls join the other babies. Runes say exactly what they do at each level.

Beta 0.9.33

Woodcutters and farmers work like the miners. The first woodcutter builds a woodcutter's lodge beside the village, and the first farmer a farmhouse with a field. Each has a chest and a head worker: talk to the Head forester or Head farmer to open it. Woodcutters fell trees, plant saplings where they cut and when trees run short, and bring the logs to the lodge. Farmers harvest and replant ripe crops, till and sow the farmhouse field, and bring the harvest in. They work wherever you are, have their own look, and friends see them too. Boats are an upgrade like an accessory: your best boat is always with you, and you sail it as soon as you walk into water. Penned and gathering animals bring produce instead of meat (cows give milk); plant eaters never bring meat, while hawks, eagles and bears can, and gatherers bring things a quarter less often. Axes and hoes have new icons.

Beta 0.9.32

Shared worlds live online: whenever a world is hosted on the game page, it is saved online every few minutes. If you join with the game ID while nobody is hosting, you open the newest copy and host it yourself; when the first host comes back, they get the newest copy too. Your hero stays your own. Every friend sees the enemies and shots around them, wherever they are, and the group shares one monster limit. Anyone can grow the village into a town or city, and it grows for everyone. Wear as many different charms as you like: their bonuses add up, and the bag's Charms worn row takes one off. Bread is made from wheat only.

Beta 0.9.31

Shared worlds: jump or swim onto a friend's boat to ride along (jump off toward land to leave), and everyone sees the soldiers sitting in a boat, the armor each player wears, and fires burning anywhere near them. Soldiers come along through realm portals. Break the frozen winter sea with a pickaxe or axe (the hole freezes over next morning). Chests have a Sort button: by type, name, value or amount. Trophies are a 2 by 2 picture of the boss and hang straight on a back wall; no shelves needed. Miners, woodcutters and farmers keep working however far away you are (woodcutters bring their logs home again, and climb over steps that blocked them). Boats say how many soldiers they carry in the shop and in crafting. The goblin forest sends a few ambushes a day instead of an endless stream, and water far from every player waits instead of flowing, so friends' games run smoother.

Beta 0.9.30

Trading with friends: stand within 5 blocks of a friend and press T (on a phone, the use button, then Trade with). A trade window opens for both of you: tap items in your bag to put them on the table, add coins, and both press Accept to swap. Changing an offer takes back both Accepts, and F no longer hands items over. Raids on your village are gentler: none before day 5, then a small chance each morning of 1 to 3 soldiers, growing by 1 or 2 every 5 days. Raiders land on open ground outside your village, never on a roof or inside your walls. Blocks go down over animals (they step aside), and tapping an old block while holding a different block swaps them, with the old one going into your bag. Chests have a Stack button that joins stacks of the same item. In shared worlds, enemies are just as active around every friend as around the host, and castle guards wake for whoever walks in. Hiring a woodcutter or farmer no longer freezes the game.

Beta 0.9.29

Split stacks: select a stack in the bag (or in a chest on a phone) and a Move slider appears with 1, Half and All; tapping another slot, dragging or Drop then moves only that many. On a computer, right-click a stack to pick up half, or right-click in a chest to send half across. Charcoal: burn a log of any wood in a furnace. Torches take a stick and a charcoal (coal works too) for four. In shared worlds everyone sees trees fall, a friend's logs pop out at the stump for everyone to see, friends who join see the host's explored map, and a player who leaves disappears with a "left the game" message.

Beta 0.9.28

Worlds can have names. Type one on the New world screen (or leave it blank), rename a world any time from Continue with the Rename button, and see the name in the save list, the pause menu and the multiplayer Recent list.

Beta 0.9.27

Grass slowly grows back over bare dirt that touches grass and is open to the air, so dug-up or placed dirt greens over in a few minutes and the grass keeps spreading. Tilled soil, and dirt under a block or under water, stay as they are. On a computer the top bar shows every button again (Bag, Craft, Army, Buildings, Full screen, the eye, Menu and Minimize); phones keep the shorter bar with the ⋯ More button.

Beta 0.9.26

The wiki has a phone layout: a bar along the bottom (Back, Home, Search, Contents, Play), a big search box with large results, a slide-out menu, recipes and tables shown as cards that fit the screen, long lists that show the first few with a Show all button, and long pages folded into sections you tap open.

Beta 0.9.25

The wiki is its own app at pumped60.github.io/dragon-amulet-wiki, with its own icon, and it works offline. Add it to your Home Screen beside the game. The Wiki link on the title screen opens it without closing the game: on Android it opens the wiki app, and on iPhone a Safari window with a Done button that takes you back.

Beta 0.9.24

Woodcutters, farmers and miners start with a wanderer: the first one you give each job becomes its head and builds the lodge, farmhouse or mine. Then hire up to 5 of each from the Quartermaster for 50 coins. Upgrading a shop changes its house: level 2 lifts the roof for a third floor with the shopkeeper's bedroom, lanterns and furniture for the trade (weapon racks and armor stands for the Blacksmith, tables and stools for the Cook, desks for the Jeweler, barrels for the Fisher and so on). Level 3 adds a balcony with a railing, a red tile roof with a turret on each corner, a banner on the roof, paintings, rugs and a showpiece for the trade.

Beta 0.9.23

Growing your village (into a town, then a city) and the report on the opposing villages (their food, gold and army, Watch a commander, gifts to villages you conquered) are in the Buildings window, under your buildings and defense posts. The Army window keeps your party, soldiers, animals, war machines, expeditions and hiring.

Beta 0.9.22

Phones: tapping a button (Bag, Army, Buildings, More and the rest) no longer pops up its name. On a computer the name still shows when you hover the mouse over it.

Beta 0.9.21

Silver armor sits between wooden and iron armor (4.5 defense, 15 silver bars), like the silver tools and weapons. If you wear iron armor, you keep it. In shared worlds, everyone sees each other's lit bombs flying and on the ground, the pieces a blast throws, and the rubble from anyone's bomb, which crumbles away after three days.

Beta 0.9.20

Phones: swiping sideways or down on a menu or the death screen can no longer take the browser back or reload the page and drop you out of the game.

Beta 0.9.19

Phones: buttons and taps on the world stay lined up after you turn the phone sideways, and small buttons are easier to hit. In the bag and in chests, hold an item for a moment to pick it up and drag it to another slot, or tap it (you see its name) and then tap the slot where it should go. In a chest, tap an item twice to send it straight across.

Beta 0.9.18

On phones, the ✕ in the top corner closes every menu and pop-up, including the pause menu, the ⋯ More menu and the eye's list, and never taps the button underneath. Tapping an item shows just its name; tap the name to see its picture and every stat. Settings has tabs (Controls, Screen, Sound, World, Computer). Under Screen you can choose what tapping an item shows (name only, short, everything or nothing) and stand the item bar and the health, mana, XP and hunger bars up and down instead of across.

Beta 0.9.17

Two treasures to find in chests. The Dragon compass shows which way the dragon's lair lies and how far; without it you can't tell. The Astrolabe shows the season, the weather and the days until the next season; without it the clock shows only the day. One compass always waits in the goblin warcamp's gold chest, the Jeweler sells astrolabes, and the test world starts with both.

Beta 0.9.16

Trees are back to their original look: the trunk reaches a round crown and the leaves sit over it.

Beta 0.9.15

The eye (under ⋯ More, or H) opens a "Show on screen" list with everything ticked: untick the item bar, health bars, info lines, mini-map or a button and it hides at once; tick it to bring it back. Hide everything hides it all in one go. In shared worlds every player sees bomb blasts and the bosses' warning marks (the Sky Ranger's wind ring and target, the Magma Knight's glowing cracks).

Beta 0.9.14

A calmer top bar: Bag, Army, Buildings, the God menu (test world), Menu and ⋯ More. Crafting is a tab at the top of the bag (C still opens it). Speed sits with the other switches in the God menu.
